citation: Department of Public Works and Highways. (2021, October 5). Laguna Lakeshore Road Network Environmental Impact Statement Report. Official copy hosted on the DENR Environmental Management Bureau EIA portal.

primarySource.accessMethod: Read the official PDF text view on 2026-11-16. No local copy or table image was retained.
sourceLocators: Table 2.44, report pp. 326-327: lake ecology transect station context and 2020 station dates.
Methods, report pp. 331-332: fish egg and larval sampling method.
Table 2.55, report pp. 367-368: fish larvae counts by family and station.
Table 2.58 and surrounding text, report pp. 385-386: seven common fish reported from a January 2014 West Bay EIA study.
Table 2.59 and surrounding text, report pp. 388-394: 19-taxon summary attributed to the report's current baseline study.

findings.scope: The report concerns the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network project corridor along West Bay, not the entire lake or all connected waters.
findings.baseline2020: The report states that its current baseline fish summary comprises 19 species, 14 families and 17 genera and labels the evidence as fish observed, reported and recorded. The listed summary is not resolved to species-by-station records, individual capture dates, voucher identifiers or a clearly described collection method for each adult-fish claim.
findings.jan2014Context: A separate paragraph attributes seven commonly caught West Bay fish to a January 2014 EIA study by EcosysCorp. The underlying 2014 study was not retrieved or independently reviewed here.
findings.ichthyoplankton: The EIS separately describes 2020 fish egg and larval sampling at 16 nearshore/offshore stations and reports family-level larval counts. Its stated method uses a bongo net and station-specific dates. This is a different evidence stream from the adult-fish summary and does not make Table 2.59's species assignments station-resolved.
findings.taxonomicQuality: The report mixes historical names and current-name notes, and its table-level taxonomic spellings, residency labels and conservation statuses were not independently validated. No species-level row was transcribed.
findings.images: The EIS contains fish photographs, including internet-sourced images; individual identity and reuse rights were not reviewed. No image was copied or approved for Bangwit.

rightsReview.finding: No open-data license or item-specific permission to republish the EIS tables or images was identified in the reviewed report text.
rightsReview.decision: Use only as a cited discovery and historical-context lead pending a separate rights review. Do not reproduce its species table, photos or structured rows in the app or a redistributed data package.

decision.reason: The West Bay project-focused EIS is a useful retrieval lead but its adult-fish table merges observed, reported and recorded claims without a verified taxon-by-station, capture-date and voucher crosswalk; reuse permission is also unverified.

nonClaims: The EIS's 19-taxon summary is not a complete Laguna de Bay checklist or proof of current presence.
The 2020 family-level fish-larvae samples do not validate the adult-fish names or the 2014 West Bay claims.
Fish photos, bait/diet claims, fishing rules, water safety, population trends and whole-lake distribution are not approved or inferred from this review.
nextActions: Locate the underlying EcosysCorp January 2014 study and any fish-by-site supporting records through a lawful public repository route.
Check whether the 2020 adult-fish claims have a separate methods appendix, site table, catch log or voucher list; assess rights before any row extraction.
Keep the Laguna de Bay research lead open and continue other Luzon regions in parallel.
